Generally, the feedback we received from those properties in direct vicinity of the site were fairly positive, and you can see the one letter on the agenda from the roughly condo corpus as well, indicating their experiences. Some of the additional feedback we had was that they appreciated knowing exactly who to contact about issues in the area and felt that issues were resolved in a very timely manner. I also wanted to share a few other pieces of information related to the communications and clarify a few points. This extension at 210 is required to allow for the completion of the new shelter on 31st Street, as I've mentioned. The new shelter is the first purpose-built shelter being developed in the province, so this is not a case where it's a cut and paste of another building from another community. In terms of process, the permit application for this development was received on May 20th and required some revisions from the applicants to meet our regulations. Those have since been provided, and we expect to issue the permit this week. So, although it has been some time since the initial announcement of the new permanent site in August of 2025, that period of time has since involved all stages of design, site considerations, tendering, award of contract, and this last month, the permit application period. I'm just providing this information to you to take advantage of the opportunity today to share the correct facts on this. We do tend to see a fair amount of misinformation. So, in summary, the request before you today is to approve an eight-month timeframe for continued use of 210 Pacific, along with the complementary lease and tax exemption, to continue as it exists today. This will allow for that longer-term purpose-built shelter to be completed. We also do have representatives from the Ministry of Social Services here today to answer any questions if you have any. With that, Mayor Block can take any questions.

Mayor Block: Thank you. Are there any questions of our administration or for the province?
Councillor Timon: Through you to Ms. Anderson, sorry. So, it didn't specify in the report any financial implications, but with this extension, is there additional cost to the city? I know there's the property tax; you talked about there were no numbers, but do you have any numbers as to what the cost is to the city?
Response: So, the cost related to that tax exemption, that's really the main piece, is approximately $14,000 a year. So, for the months, someone could do the math.
Councillor Timon: Okay, so there are no other costs for the city for this extension?
Response: No, unless we see some sort of maintenance requirement that comes up that's above the threshold that we would deal with as a landlord. So, we haven't had that yet.
Councillor Timon: Okay, thank you.

Councillor Parker: Thank you. This question is kind of in response to the letter from the Remai Modern. They've asked, I guess, essentially, you're looking for confirmation that the services that we have in place as far as the community safety plan will remain in place. I just want to be able to give them that confirmation.
Response: Thank you. Yes, that was addressed earlier today on the agenda with the community safety plan report. So, I believe community council approved that request.
Councillor Parker: Thank you very much.

Councillor Kelleher: Thank you, and through you, Your Worship, just to the administration again, on the note of the letter that came through asking about the delays in permitting. I think it's 23 days. Is that about right? And is that within the service standard that the city holds for processing those types of claims?
Response: Yes, so we received it on May 20th. We reviewed it and sent it back to the applicant to make revisions, so part of the 23 days has been in our hands, part has been in their hands. But that is well within our service standards.
Councillor Kelleher: Okay, and then there is just a second piece that was, sort of asking if the city could do what it can to make sure that the project is completed on time, on budget, and...
Response: I think you've identified that we don't have those roles in this project. We don't have that level of control in someone else's procured project. But I do know from our discussions with the ministry and their contract, they did include milestones that they're requiring to be met. That's a common practice to ensure that it's not delayed unnecessarily and can be expedited as quickly as possible, so they've done that in their contract. But beyond that, the city doesn't have a role to enforce someone else's contractor through a process.
Councillor Kelleher: All right, so we could get information reports, and then that would be about it, correct?
Response: Correct.
Councillor Kelleher: Okay, thank you. Those are my questions.

Mayor Block: Don't see any more questions. Are there any comments? I don't see any, and I'll ask for a mover and seconder for this one. Moved by Councillor Pearce, seconded by Councillor Davies. If there is no further discussion, I'll call the question. Is anyone opposed? And that carries. I think I want to track, and we go to 10.3.2. Shaw Centre score clock and timing equipment: request for additional funding. I'll turn this over to our administration.

Matthew Learned, Director of Recreation and Community Development: Good afternoon, Your Worship, members of council. This report seeks council approval for an additional $187,000 for the Shaw Centre score clock and timing equipment project, increasing the total project budget from $848,000 to $1.035 million. Funding for this project was approved in May of 2025, based on a high-level cost estimate. Following completion of the procurement process and detailed negotiations with the successful proponent, the final project cost has now been confirmed. The resulting budget shortfall is primarily attributable to cost escalation and the difference between the original planning level estimate and current market pricing for this specialized equipment. The project remains essential to the facility, as the existing score clock and timing system is at the end of its useful life, and it supports the Shaw Centre's ability to host sanctioned aquatic competitions. Administration is recommending that the additional funding be provided from the Leisure Services Equipment Replacement Reserve, which has sufficient capacity to absorb the increase without affecting any of the other approved capital projects. The timing of this request is important. Approval at today's meeting will allow the work to proceed during the summer months, when usage of the 50-meter pool is at its lowest. Completing the installation during this window will minimize impacts on the user groups, reduce disruption to programming, and ensure the facility is ready for the upcoming competition season. Administration therefore recommends the approval of the additional $187,000 to complete the project. With that, administration will be pleased to answer any questions you have.

Ms. Anderson: Thank you. The area concept plan for the next development, an infill development in the Homewood area, is currently under review by administration. The Homewood Urban Centre Concept Plan provides for an urban centre, a residential neighbourhood, and a business park with a regional commercial area. The total concept plan area includes just over 445 hectares or just over 1,100 acres. It was estimated to accommodate a population of approximately 17,500 people and employment for over 8,000 people. Technical reviews for the concept plan are ongoing, and these include reviews of policy, land use, traffic impact assessment, wetland mitigation plans, and site servicing analysis. Referrals are sent out to numerous civic departments, external agencies, and school boards, and those are also ongoing.

Once the technical reviews are substantially complete, public engagement will be conducted, followed by reports from administration for consideration by Municipal Planning Commission and by City Council at a future public hearing. At this time, the concept plan is anticipated to be brought forward to a public hearing in Q1 of 2027. In 2024, as Council will know, the Province of Saskatchewan announced funding for a new joint use high school in the homewood urban center, which would accommodate both a public and a Catholic high school, each anticipated to have approximately 1,800 students. Planning for the new joint use high school has been underway, concurrently with the review of the area concept plan. Tendering of the school project is expected to occur in spring 2027, with construction starting later that year. To ensure the site for the high schools is ready for construction as planned next year, there is a need to advance limited site preparation and the servicing work at this time, in advance of concept plan approval. Construction activities would include a sanitary sewer trunk located south of the proposed joint use high school site for approximately 250 meters from the main sewer trunk; associated shallow services, including sanitary, storm, and water mains, located south of the proposed high school site; and roadway construction located south of the site as well. This type of servicing typically does not begin until after a concept plan is approved for a neighborhood. However, review of the related technical studies for the concept plan have advanced sufficiently for us to confirm that the proposed work can be designed and installed to meet City of Saskatoon standards. Facilitating this work ahead of the concept plan approval will ensure that the site is ready in time for the planned construction of the high schools to start in late 2027. Subject to approval by City Council, dream would undertake the construction of these services in accordance with our procurement policies. Advancing these projects ahead of the concept plan approval will help us to ensure that the important community project of the high schools can advance in a timely manner and meet the goals of the province and the city to ensure that's in place. With that, Marblek, I can take any questions.
